title: Nano-subscription stitching: session & quota heuristics
content:
Goal: sketch a cheap, low-friction nano-subscription (micro buck-per-month) that maps to session credits and stays economical across hosted + dedicated.

Design constraints / goals:
- sticky: tiers that are obvious to a product (per-user monthly anchor).
- simple: users think in sessions or ‘quick calls’ not tokens.
- cost-protective: avoid heavy subsidy for noisy token-heavy users.
- interoperable: works with existing per-token billing as overage.

Key heuristics to test (back-of-envelope):
1) Session credit definition (one unified unit):
   - baseline session credit = 1 credit per conversation up to 1k tokens (prompt+resp).
   - overages: +1 credit per additional 1k tokens (round up).
   - rationale: aligns with common short chat UX and reduces need to surface tokens.

2) Token-to-credit mapping (quick math):
   - avg short convo = 600 tokens -> 1 credit.
   - avg long convo = 3200 tokens -> 4 credits.
   - if we price 1 credit at $0.01 (example), then a long convo costs $0.04 in sticker.

3) Unit economics baseline (hosted):
   assumptions: avg token cost to Redwood (amortized infra + model) = $0.0000025 / token (2.5e-6),
   - short convo (600 tokens) cost = 600 * 2.5e-6 = $0.0015 => 1 credit must cover $0.0015 infra cost + margin + acquisition overhead.
   - set retail 1-credit = $0.01 => gross margin large (good for virality).
   - breakeven credit-price if we target 60% gross margin: retail * (1 - margin) = cost => retail = cost / 0.4 = $0.00375. So $0.01 is conservative.

4) Subscription tier sketches (examples to test):
   - Nano: $1/month = 100 credits (intro/viral) -> $0.01/credit (covers average short conv and leaves room).
   - Micro: $5/month = 625 credits -> $0.008/credit (anchored to use-case: frequent short queries).
   - Starter: $20/month = 3500 credits -> $0.0057/credit (for small teams).
   - Overage: per-credit $0.0125 (higher than lowest tier to encourage upgrades).
   Rationale: give perceived bulk discount while keeping unit economics positive.

5) Concurrency & SLO implications (ops):
   - credits are logical; we must still enforce per-request rate limits to protect latency SLOs.
   - micro-subs should not be allowed to queue huge parallel bursts (abuse vector).
   - suggest adding a soft concurrency cap per seat (e.g., 5 rps) with burst tokens.

6) Dedicated customers / amortization nuance:
   - For Dedicated, marginal infra cost per token is lower for committed pools. Need alternate mapping: credits -> committed-unit-hours used up.
   - Option: allow converting credits to GPU-second coupons for dedicated customers with a separate conversion table. Keeps accounting clean.

7) Promo & onboarding mechanics:
   - free-trial: 200 starter credits for signup (expires in 30 days).
   - usage nudges: show "x credits remaining translates to ~y short chats" in UI.

8) Edge cases & open questions:
   - system messages / tool calls — do they count towards token budget? (Proposal: yes, count total tokens consumed by request+plugins to avoid hidden cost gaps.)
   - very high token single requests (file summarization) — charging by credits could be confusing; provide explicit token pricing or a "large job" path.
   - idle session or multi-turn with long KV cache reuse — do we charge only on generation tokens? (Prefer counting consumed tokens only but investigate prefix caching discounts).

9) Quick sensitivity: what if average tokens per short convo is 1.2k (not 600)?
   - new cost per short convo = 1200 * 2.5e-6 = $0.003 -> if 1 credit remains $0.01, margin still ok. But if cost jumps (e.g., for larger models or LLM price increases), tier discounts need cap to avoid subsidy.

10) Implementation notes / telemetry to capture for experiments:
   - record token_count_total, credit_consumed, convo_type (short/long/LLM-batch), model_family, region, plan_id, seat_id.
   - add experiment flag: map tokens->credits by round_up( tokens / credit_token_bucket ) where credit_token_bucket is per-plan variable.

11) Product language / UX copy quick drafts:
   - "Nano Plan — 100 quick chats / month" (instead of tokens).
   - tooltip: "Quick chat = ~1 short question + answer (~600 tokens). Longer chats use more credits."

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Run 7-day sample of active users: compute token distribution per convo and percentile cutoffs (50/75/90). (Jira: JIRA-ENG-987)
- A/B: show credits-first vs tokens-first onboarding copy and measure conversion/time-to-first-pay.
- Pilot nano-plan in EU region (lower card churn historically) with 2000 signups.

Notes to self: keep the mapping simple to avoid support friction. If we need finer control, hide complexity in conversion tables on backend and present only "credits" to end users.

Unresolved: target gross margin per-credit (currently using 60%) — discuss with finance.

Quick links: Slack thread #pricing-experiments, confluence CONFLUENCE-1234 (analysis stub), PR #22 (implementation sketch).

End of scratchpad.
